This vignette walks through a complete prediction workflow for one
calibration **pair** -- manta tow vs ReefScan Surface coral cover, at the
tow level -- using the package's building blocks:

1. `rosetta_models()` to look up a model's fitting conventions,
2. `rosetta_posterior()` to load the posterior draws bundled with the
   package,
3. a `pred*From*()` wrapper (or the generic `rosetta_predict()`) to turn
   those draws into a prediction curve,
4. plotting the result.

RosettaGBR does not fit models, but it ships the saved posterior draws for
all 52 BR-04 calibration models, so everything below runs as-is.

```{r setup}
library(RosettaGBR)
library(ggplot2)
```

## 1. Look up the model

Every BR-04 calibration model is documented in the registry returned by
`rosetta_models()`: one row per model, keyed by the model name. Look up
both directions of the manta/RS-Surface coral-cover pair:

```{r}
rosetta_models() |>
  subset(model_name %in% c("manta_from_surf_tow", "surf_from_manta_tow")) |>
  subset(select = c(model_name, family, level, response_variable, predictor_variable, link))
```

Both directions are `"beta"` family (coral cover is a proportion) at
`"tow"` level, but they use *different* links (see the registry's `link`
column above): `manta_from_surf_tow` is `link = "loglog"`
(`mu = exp(-exp(-eta))`) while `surf_from_manta_tow` is `link = "logit"`
(`mu = plogis(eta)`), with no offset (coral cover models have no effort
term, unlike the COTS count models). You don't need to branch on this by
hand: `predBetaCurve()` reads the link from `attr(post, "link")` on the
posterior (defaulting to `"logit"` when that attribute is absent), so the
same call works for every Beta coral model. This tells us what each
model's `x` and response are:

- **`manta_from_surf_tow`**: predicts manta tow `perc_hard` (response)
  from RS Surface `pct_HC_surf` (predictor).
- **`surf_from_manta_tow`**: the reverse direction -- predicts RS Surface
  `pct_HC_surf` from manta `perc_hard`.

Fitting a *separate* model per direction (rather than algebraically
inverting one fit) is deliberate: a Beta-regression fit of Y-on-X is not
the exact inverse of a fit of X-on-Y, so both directions were fit
independently.

## 2. Load the posterior

Each model's posterior draws are bundled with the package and returned by
`rosetta_posterior()`: a numeric matrix with one row per posterior draw
and, for a Beta-family model, columns `alpha`, `beta` and `phi` (this is the
same contract [RosettaCOTS](https://github.com/Scott-Foster/RosettaCOTS)
uses).

```{r}
post <- rosetta_posterior("manta_from_surf_tow")
dim(post)
head(post)
attr(post, "link")
```

The `"link"` attribute (not a column) is how the prediction functions know
to use the loglog inverse link for this particular model.

## 3. Predict a calibration curve

Call the wrapper function named after the model (`manta_from_surf_tow` ->
`predMantaFromSurfTow()`), supplying a grid of predictor values. With no
`post` argument the bundled posterior is used:

```{r}
x_seq <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 100)
pred_manta <- predMantaFromSurfTow(x = x_seq)
pred_manta
```

The returned tibble has one row per `x` and five prediction columns:

- **`mean`**: posterior mean of the fitted curve (population-level,
  group/random effects marginalized to zero).
- **`lo95`/`hi95`**: 95% credible interval on that mean curve.
- **`pi_lo95`/`pi_hi95`**: 95% *prediction* interval for a single new
  observation at that `x` (always at least as wide as the credible
  interval -- see `?predBetaCurve` for why this is enforced).

Equivalently, via the generic dispatcher (useful when looping over many
models by name rather than calling named functions one at a time):

```{r}
pred_manta2 <- rosetta_predict("manta_from_surf_tow", x = x_seq)
all.equal(pred_manta$mean, pred_manta2$mean, tolerance = 0.01)
```

(The two agree to Monte Carlo noise only: each call independently
subsamples the posterior for the prediction-interval simulation.)

## 4. Plot the calibration curve

```{r}
ggplot(pred_manta, aes(x, mean)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = pi_lo95, ymax = pi_hi95), fill = "grey70", alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo95, ymax = hi95), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  labs(
    x = "RS Surface % hard coral (predictor)",
    y = "Manta tow % hard coral (predicted)",
    title = "predMantaFromSurfTow()",
    subtitle = "Mean (line), 95% credible interval (dark band), 95% prediction interval (light band)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## 5. The other direction of the pair

The reverse-direction model, `surf_from_manta_tow`, has an *independent*
posterior (its own `alpha`/`beta`/`phi`) and predicts the opposite way: RS
Surface cover as a function of manta cover.

```{r}
pred_surf <- predSurfFromMantaTow(x = x_seq)

ggplot(pred_surf, aes(x, mean)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = pi_lo95, ymax = pi_hi95), fill = "grey70", alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo95, ymax = hi95), fill = "darkorange", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  labs(
    x = "Manta tow % hard coral (predictor)",
    y = "RS Surface % hard coral (predicted)",
    title = "predSurfFromMantaTow()"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## 6. Using your own posterior

Every wrapper also accepts a `post` argument, so you can supply posterior
draws from your own fit of the same model. It must be a matrix (or data
frame) with columns `alpha`, `beta` and `phi`, and optionally a `"link"`
attribute:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
my_post <- readRDS("path/to/my_posterior.RDS")
predMantaFromSurfTow(my_post, x = x_seq)
```

- `?rosetta_models` for the full 52-model registry and its columns
  (family, level, offset/eps conventions, grouping, etc.).
- `?rosetta_posterior` for what each bundled posterior contains.
- `?predBetaCurve` / `?predNegBinCurve` / `?predBinomialCurve` for the
  three underlying prediction engines, including how prediction intervals
  are constructed for the two COTS families (which this coral-cover
  example, being Beta, doesn't need an `offset`/`size` argument for).
- The package README for the relationship to RosettaCOTS and the full
  list of 52 `pred*From*()` functions.
